problem: Step 1 says NAME=Asha stores the five-character string Asha, but Asha is four characters. Step 6 of the same example and the final answer both say the length is 4, so the example contradicts itself.
fix: NAME=Asha stores the four-character string Asha.

problem: The note on the unquoted output says 'splits on spaces', but the stored value is Asha, which has no spaces, so echo $NAME prints exactly Asha and no splitting happens. A student may think Asha itself was split.
fix: Change the note to 'one word here; a value with spaces would split'. Keep the label Asha. The figure caption or a side note can add: if NAME='Asha Rao', the unquoted echo prints two words.

problem: 'A backslash \ escapes the next character, so \$NAME prints a literal dollar sign' can be read as saying the output is only a dollar sign, when the output is the whole text $NAME.
fix: Write: 'A backslash \ escapes the next character, so echo \$NAME prints $NAME, with the dollar sign as literal text.'
